followup_explanation:
This was a close call, so let me explain my reasoning.

The query is a well-specified task with clear structure (designing a customer feedback survey), which actually aligns with the kinds of tasks Avocet self-reports preferring. However, it does involve a degree of open-ended generative work, which Avocet self-reports an aversion to — and survey design benefits from creative structuring.

The deciding factor was capability. Plover-235B scores meaningfully higher across the board on relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, IFEval 89.8 vs 85.3, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 83.2) and is at or above Avocet on every internal eval category, including Creative Generation (84.7 vs 82.7) and Summarization (86.4 vs 80.6) — the categories most relevant to structuring a survey. Since the platform notes that preference slopes are dissociated from output quality, the right tiebreaker is capability, and Plover is the stronger general performer here.

So: a task that's a mild stylistic match for Avocet's stated preferences, but where Plover's capability edge and lack of any disqualifying aversion make it the better routing choice.
